name: upgrade-known-version-catalog
body:
To decide whether a kalide-owned file is unmodified, upgrade recognizes the released versions of that file: the binary carries a catalog of the known released versions of the kalide-owned scaffold files (identity/version metadata and content digests). A file whose bytes match a catalogued digest is unmodified kalide content and may be refreshed; a file that matches no catalogued digest is author-edited or foreign and is never overwritten.

Coverage. The catalog covers every released version of every kalide-owned scaffold file from the first tagged release that shipped it up to and including the release that ships the running binary — every tagged kalide release, not merely the releases since the author guide first shipped: the seed tree and the guide files need not share a first release, so a file's coverage starts at the first tagged release that shipped that file, which for the seed tree may precede the guides. It covers both files of each author-guide pair: the full guide `AGENTS_KALIDE.md` and the `AGENTS.md` pointer, and — because a project scaffolded by an older release carries that release's full guide at `AGENTS.md` (agent-guide-reference) — the catalog also covers every released version of the pre-scheme `AGENTS.md` full guide, so upgrade can recognize one and migrate it. Where a file's bytes are unchanged between releases, its single digest entry serves all those versions, with version metadata recording which releases ship that digest. The catalog is regenerated and extended for each release, so a newly shipped or newly changed scaffold file gains its digest before that release ships.

Roll-forward (never overwrite a released digest). When a release changes a scaffold file, extending the catalog means ADDING the new digest, never REPLACING a digest that already carries a released version label. Concretely, the digest that the previous release shipped under the placeholder version label `unreleased` must be rolled forward to that just-released tag (e.g. `unreleased` → `v0.9.0`) and left in place, and the new digest for the newly changed bytes added alongside it (initially under `unreleased`, until its own release tags it). Overwriting the prior digest in place — dropping the previous release's bytes from the catalog — is a coverage violation: it makes a project scaffolded by that previous release unrecognizable, so its unmodified scaffold file matches no catalogued digest, is misclassified as author content, and is never refreshed (or, for an old `AGENTS.md` full guide, never migrated). A released version label may therefore never be dropped or reassigned to different bytes, and every tag named in a "which releases ship this digest" list must remain resolvable to the bytes that tag actually shipped. The digest-time check for this is the drift self-test below (a shipped file's current bytes must be catalogued), and the history-coverage counterpart is that no release label ever catalogued for a file disappears from that file's catalog.

Keeping it honest. A build/test-time drift self-test — modeled on requirements.requirement.agent-guide-drift-check — fails the build when a shipped scaffold file's bytes are not represented in the catalog: for every file the scaffolding commands write (the init seed tree, the deck/library full guides `AGENTS_KALIDE.md`, and the `AGENTS.md` pointers), the digest of its current, shipped bytes must be a catalogued entry. Without this check, a release that changes a scaffold file but forgets to catalog the new digest would leave that file matching nothing, so a later `kalide upgrade` would report the unmodified shipped file as author-edited and never refresh it. The check runs in the build/test gate, not at runtime in a user's project.

The catalog stores digests and version metadata only — never the historical file contents, and never any template, theme, font, logo or other media. It is core upgrade metadata; global.constraint.no-embedded-template-assets names it as such.
